title: Ultra-processed foods cause weight gain and increased energy intake associated with reduced chewing frequency: a randomized, open-label, crossover study
authors: Hamano S, Sawada M, Aihara M, Sakurai Y, Sekine R, Usami S, et al.
followUp: 1 week on each diet with a 2-week washout
population: Japanese men with overweight or obesity at the University of Tokyo Hospital
funder: Funding statement not read: the publisher's full text and PDF returned HTTP 403 to automated access, and the article is absent from PubMed Central. Publisher-deposited Crossref metadata name the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (B) 21H02976.
result: Open-label crossover; meals matched for total energy and macronutrients. During the ultra-processed period participants gained 1.1 kg more (95% CI 0.2 to 2.0; P = 0.021) and ate 813.5 kcal/day more (342.4 to 1284.7; P = 0.0041); chews per kilocalorie were lower (P = 0.016). Results read from the PubMed abstract.
